doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

title: Why Sidran does so many things in music
summary: He says he is a jazz fan at heart; piano, radio and writing are all ways through the jazz life, legs on a stool.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well because at heart I’m just a huge jazz fan. It’s all I ever wanted to do was be involved in the music and these are all different aspects of how I got involved in the music. So to me it’s all kind of the same thing. I mean playing piano is something I’ve done since I was six years old and it doesn’t feel any different than doing an interview on the radio or whatever. All those things that we tend to think of as separate really aren’t at all, they’re just ways to go through the jazz life, which isn’t an easy process as we all know, and so it actually made it simpler for me, not more complicated, to have more legs on the stool that was supporting me.

I like that analogy of legs on a stool. I know, I think of Kenny Davern, the marvelous clarinet player. And he somehow made a living just being a clarinet player. Not — no studio work, he was in a big band for a very short time and he said no I’m not going to do that.
